recommended_next_phase: 149O.20L.7O.2L.3 -- narrowest repair of the recover scope/provenance defect: remove the recover subcommand in favor of the in-process retry mechanism 149O.20L.7O.2L's own architecture already specified, or obtain an explicit architecture/contract amendment naming a human-entry recovery path and defining a provenance-binding requirement before re-implementing. Do not proceed to HMIC v1.7 source-scope evolution until this is repaired and independently re-verified.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2L.2 is a verification-only phase (no real Trust-Enrollment effect performed; no repair performed). It independently verified scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py and scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py (implemented by 149O.20L.7O.2L.1) against primary source only -- HHCE-001 v1.1 and HPSE-001 v1.1 contract text, the six named core writer modules (confirmed byte-identical against an isolated git worktree fixed at the pre-2L.1 phase-entry commit d4c699e5), and 149O.20L.7O.2L's own architecture-freeze document -- never trusting 2L.1's own tests, report, comments, or its claimed +2 HMIC delta as an oracle. Independent CLI grammar reconstruction confirmed: hardware script subcommands enroll/recover/revoke, enroll has no caller-supplied credential-identity flags, recover requires all five identity fields as human-typed CLI strings; principal/signer script subcommands enroll-principal/revoke-principal/enroll-signer/revoke-signer, with no root-override flag exposed on any subcommand of either script (path-containment confirmed). AST inspection confirmed thin-wrapper status for both scripts: no json/fcntl primitives, no reimplemented parsing/validation/identity-derivation/locking/persistence/duplicate-resolution/revocation logic; every mutating call is a single pass-through into the unmodified core writer. Live instrumentation (not mere output-checking) confirmed: declined confirmation on enroll/recover produces zero register_credential calls and zero registry writes; recover makes zero calls into the hardware ceremony seam; enroll-signer's two-lock critical section is acquired and released in the correct nested order (hw_acquire, bind_acquire, bind_release, hw_release) across disposable tmp_path roots, confirming HPSE-REQ-057/HHCE-REQ-037 continuity live, not merely by AST assertion. No DeploymentBinding file is created by any hardware-script operation; neither script references create_deployment_binding, certify(, or activate_hatp_mandatory. No secret-like CLI flag exists on either script. Independent recovery-provenance analysis produced a Blocking finding: HHCE-001 v1.1 never mentions 'recover' anywhere in its text (HHCE-REQ-015 names exactly register_credential/revoke_credential as the writer's only mutating operations); 149O.20L.7O.2L's own architecture-freeze document explicitly authorized, for the hardware script, only '(register/revoke ...; never caller-supplied credential ID/public key)' and explicitly described the intended recovery mechanism as an in-process retry of register_credential() using evidence 'already held by the caller' from the same failed attempt -- 'no additional recovery state machine is required ... not by a new mechanism this phase needs to invent.' 2L.1 instead implemented a separate, third CLI subcommand accepting fully human-typed signer_key_id/provider_profile/protocol_name/algorithm/public_key_hex values with zero binding to any actual completed hardware ceremony. A fresh, independently-authored test (test_recover_accepts_fully_fabricated_evidence_with_no_prior_ceremony) demonstrates this concretely: fabricated identity values that were never produced by any enroll_credential() call are accepted by recover --assume-yes and persisted as an authoritative, active HardwareCredentialRecord, exit code 0. This directly contradicts enroll's own module-docstring invariant that credential identity is never caller-supplied, for the one subcommand described as its exception -- an exception 2L's own architecture document never authorized and in fact affirmatively contradicted. Per this phase's own adjudication instructions, this is classified Blocking (unauthorized public-surface scope expansion combined with an unauthenticated arbitrary-credential-import capability). All other verified surfaces are CLEAN: enroll and revoke (hardware) and all four principal/signer operations are each explicitly, individually authorized by 2L's architecture document section 18. Independent HMIC-REQ-052 analysis (fresh AST import-graph walk, not trusted from 2L.1) confirmed both scripts' entire reachable pcae.core.* import surface remains inside the current HMIC v1.6 frozen 36-file set, with no hidden dependency found (explicitly checked for a repeat of the historical paths.py under-count); both scripts independently answer YES to HMIC-REQ-052's own authority-sensitivity test, confirming the exact future delta as +2 (36 -> 38) once the Blocking finding is repaired. The current active Dell certification remains valid for its own currently-deployed identity (unaffected by Mac-local, not-yet-HMIC-bound new scripts), and per architecture the new scripts must not be used against Dell before an HMIC v1.7 scope evolution -- which in any case cannot responsibly proceed while this Blocking finding stands unrepaired. A fresh, independently-authored verification suite of 20 tests was written (does not import or extend any 2L.1 test file) and passes 20/20. fast_green was run twice under normal host conditions and its raw results preserved: current tree 333 failed / 8320 passed / 8 skipped / 12 errors; an isolated git worktree fixed at the pre-2L.1 phase-entry commit (d4c699e5) 334 failed / 8240 passed / 7 skipped / 12 errors. A full node-ID diff of both raw FAILED/ERROR lists found exactly one test present as a failure only in the current run (tests/test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_audit_verify_cli); re-run in isolation outside the -n auto parallel split, it passes cleanly -- confirmed as a pre-existing pytest-xdist worker-ordering flake, not attributable to 2L.1 or 2L.2. The remaining 333 (current) / 334 (fixed) failures are identical, pre-existing historical-baseline-drift debt (stale phase-entry-commit self-checks accumulated across dozens of earlier phases, entirely unrelated to Trust-Enrollment) present on both sides of the comparison and out of this phase's scope to repair. Zero attributable regressions confirmed by direct node-ID diff against the fixed pre-2L.1 worktree, 0 failed newly attributable to this phase's own changes. Final verdict: C -- NOT VERIFIED: HARDWARE-ENROLLMENT RECOVERY AUTHORITY DEFECT (Blocking, preserved not repaired per this phase's own governing instructions). No HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding was created; no physical FIDO2/PIV hardware was touched (every writer/provider interaction in this phase's own test suite uses disposable tmp_path state and a monkeypatched synthetic FIDO2 seam); no HMIC certification action was performed; the Dell host was not connected to or mutated; HATP was not activated; runtime remained Observed/observe/unavailable throughout (confirmed via pcae runtime inspect). pcae health healthy, pcae check passed, pcae status coherence coherent, pcae doctor task-memory warnings (pre-existing, unrelated), pcae push check clean pre-finalization, pcae notify status Telegram configured.
